originality.rationale: The main primary article proves the universal Godbersen inequality and its equality characterization, rather than a complete reflected coefficient profile on a symmetric-base frustum family. A second primary article treats general linear combinations and unbalanced difference bodies, not this family. The closest public mathematical record treats exactly the same frustum geometry but a distinct Santaló/Mahler invariant; a second treats a truncated simplex whose asymmetric base and coefficient formula do not imply the current all-shapes result. Complete relevant source sections and both records' mathematical RESULT texts were read. Aliases and limiting cases were searched. No covering implication identified, subject to older unindexed literature.
residual_risks: Exact difference-body profiles of symmetric-base truncated cones could have appeared in unindexed classical convex-geometric literature even if the searched records do not surface them.
The 2024 thesis on surface-area inequalities for pyramids was not available as complete text; visible excerpts do not decide whether it contains a reflected-volume endpoint identity.
Dimension-two affine coincidences with known truncated-triangle computations are not claimed to be new; the all-dimensional symmetric-base universality and crossover are the focus.

value.rationale: The quantity is the entire natural reflected mixed-volume profile entering sharp Godbersen and Rogers--Shephard inequalities. A centered homothetic frustum is a standard geometric family rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; allowing any centrally symmetric convex base, even nonsmooth, gives a nontrivial shape-independent structural theorem. The exact strict interpolation of all mixed coefficients and the dimension-dependent logistic crossover between pyramid and prism endpoints offer interpretable quantitative benchmarks beyond a textbook volume computation. No broad universal inequality is misclaimed.
